# Tiltmeter

> Tiltmeter turns API changes into pull requests in the code that still uses them. An API provider publishes one signed change notice; Tiltmeter finds the code that still calls what changed, adapts it in a sandbox and opens a pull request, before the shutdown date instead of after. Its open-source (MIT) core also works for developers on its own: `tiltmeter scan` finds code that still uses API changes that already shipped, `tiltmeter check` learns the shape of the JSON APIs a project calls and warns CI and agents (over MCP) when one changes, and `tiltmeter fix` opens the pull request that adapts the code.

Try it with `uvx tiltmeter scan` in any repository, or install with `pip install tiltmeter` (Python 3.12 or later). It runs locally with one SQLite file and no account. No API spec is needed: the contract is learned from responses.

## Plans

- Developers: free and open source (MIT): the CLI, the GitHub Action and the MCP server
- Teams: per repository, in early access, for companies that depend on many third-party APIs: a GitHub App across the organization that covers private repositories, a view of every API their services call and what changed, alerts when a provider announces a change, and fixes included
- API providers: priced by the size of the customer base; design partners get their first migration free. Signed notices, pull requests in their users' repositories under the provider's name, and a tracker of every merge. https://tiltmeter.dev/providers/
- Contact: hello@tiltmeter.dev

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/getting-started.md): install, record a baseline and catch a breaking change against a fake API in about five minutes
- [Configuration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/configuration.md): every option in `tiltmeter.yaml`
- [Scan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/scan.md): `uvx tiltmeter scan` checks a repository, with no configuration and no network, against a catalog of API changes that already shipped, and prints each affected line with the command that fixes it. The catalog is at https://tiltmeter.dev/catalog/api-changes.json; Tiltmeter drafted its entries from public documentation and no provider signed them
- [Agents and MCP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/agents.md): the MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, LangChain and other clients
- [Fixing code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/fix.md): how `tiltmeter fix` adapts code in a worktree and opens a pull request
- [CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/ci.md): exit codes and jobs for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and cron
- [How it works](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/how-it-works.md): shapes, baselines and what counts as drift
- [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/faq.md)
- [Provider notices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/notices.md): providers publish signed change notices; customers get a pull request per change that affects their code, or follow a provider's OpenAPI spec directly
- [API change notices, v1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tiltmeter-dev/tiltmeter/main/docs/notice-spec.md): the open notice and feed format, signatures and the rules for readers, with JSON Schemas at https://tiltmeter.dev/schemas/api-change-notice/v1.json and https://tiltmeter.dev/schemas/api-change-feed/v1.json

## Pages

- [Home](https://tiltmeter.dev/): what Tiltmeter does for API providers and teams, traction and plans
- [For developers](https://tiltmeter.dev/developers/): drift checks, agents over MCP, fixes and CI, for a project that calls third-party APIs
- [For API providers](https://tiltmeter.dev/providers/): publishing signed change notices and getting the fixes to customers

## For agents

- [Full reference](https://tiltmeter.dev/llms-full.txt): setup steps, commands, MCP tools, drift types and exit codes in one file
- [Migration tracker](https://tiltmeter.dev/migrations/): the pull requests Tiltmeter opened in public repositories to fix code using API changes, grouped by provider, with their status on GitHub; the data is at https://tiltmeter.dev/migrations/status.json. Tiltmeter drafted these change notices from public documentation; no provider signed or endorsed them
